verdict.rationale: PayPal exposes a broad set of REST APIs, an agent toolkit, and an MCP server covering orders, invoices, subscriptions, refunds, disputes, catalog management, and cart operations, giving AI-native users substantial programmatic parity with UI actions. However, key agentic-commerce features (Agent Ready, Store Sync, ACP/UCP checkout) are gated behind Braintree accounts, form-based approval, or Google enablement rather than being self-serve/open, and Store Sync is scoped only to US physical goods in USD, meaning many UI-available merchant actions aren't uniformly API-accessible. missing for 10: evidence that all UI-available merchant/consumer actions (not just orders/refunds/disputes/catalog) are API-exposed without gating, self-serve access without approval forms, and support beyond US physical goods/USD.
